A guided tour of the
Newspeak semantics in Lean

The formalization is not a second, smaller language. It is the quasi-formal specification made explicit enough for a proof assistant to reject gaps. This tour starts with the architecture, teaches only the Lean notation you need, and then descends one layer at a time.

Start with the map What changed in the prose?
Complete language model Machine-checked properties Beginner-first explanations Every source file included
00

Before the notation

Read it as a precise story, not as a program

Lean serves two roles here. Some definitions are executable algorithms. Others are mathematical relations describing which transitions are legal. Theorems connect the two and prove that the legal answer is unique where Newspeak requires determinism.

→
Your reading rule: first ask “what concept is being named?” Then ask “is this data, a computation, a relation, or a proof?” You can ignore the proof script on a first pass.
structureRecord-shaped data

A value with named fields: a program, heap, class, frame, or certificate.

inductiveAlternatives or rules

A closed set of cases: syntax nodes, transition rules, or derivations.

defComputation

An executable function or a named mathematical predicate.

theoremChecked claim

A proposition plus a proof Lean's kernel has accepted.

01

The feedback loop

What the Lean work changed—or forced us to make explicit—in the LaTeX

There is no historical LaTeX revision in the enclosing Git repository, so this is a semantic reconstruction from the current prose, the Lean design record, and their modification chronology. Draft 0.14 now incorporates the three places where the completed Lean development had moved ahead of draft 0.13.

Reflected in LaTeX

Identity became part of the semantics

Slot, declaration, method, activation, class-body, object-literal, event, pause-token, and source-site identities are no longer informal names. Stable identity is what makes reflection, layout migration, caches, frame copying, and source correlation stateable.

Reflected in LaTeX

The static/runtime boundary sharpened

Mixin definitions live in P; classes and their object representations live in H. This answered the reflection question: replace static definitions transactionally, but continue to represent mixins as ordinary heap objects when the language observes them.

Reflected in LaTeX

Control became materialized state

An activation now retains provenance, current receiver, optional current class, continuation, home method, current term, and control location. That is the minimum needed for resumable exceptions, arbitrary stack editing, and return to normal full-speed execution.

Reflected in LaTeX

Finite domains replaced implicit function spaces

Reflection and GC need to enumerate what exists. The model therefore uses finite stores with exact domains for heap records, environments, methods, source tables, and caches. This is what makes allInstancesOf: and all mixin applications precise.

Reflected in LaTeX

Sequential “phases” became composable relations

Receiver/argument order, invocation, returns, closures, slot access, class creation, initialization, literals, and top-level entry are distinct relations. Lean then proves their cases are disjoint and their union deterministic.

Reflected in LaTeX

Absence is not a fake object

Top-level activations genuinely lack a current class and home method. Lean's Option types exposed places where inventing a sentinel such as Top would silently grant meaning that the language does not have.

Reflected in LaTeX

Weakness was separated from ordinary reachability

WeakArray cells and WeakMap ephemerons cannot be modeled as normal slots. The prose now has an optional GC layer with unconditional strong edges, conditional map edges, atomic clearing, and identity non-reuse.

Reflected in LaTeX

The front end became a real semantic pipeline

The PEG, concrete-tree projection, stable source identification, surface well-formedness, elaboration, program derivation, and independently checked core image are separate stages. This replaced the former hand-wave from grammar to annotated core.

Reflected in LaTeX

Metacircularity acquired an admission boundary

The parser, elaborator, compiler, and Simulator are ordinary Newspeak objects. Their outputs are admitted only when certificates connect them to fixed PEG/core/VM semantics. No special “install compiler” transition is needed.

Synchronized in 0.14

The proof status is current

The obsolete “remaining metatheory” paragraph has been replaced by a machine-checked status section covering PEG and elaboration determinism, sequential preservation, lookup equivalence, reflection commutation, Simulator refinement, and GC fixed points.

Synchronized in 0.14

Grammar admissibility is executable

The prose now supplements pegOK with the finite certificate for defined references, absence of leading cycles, and non-nullable repetition operands, together with its soundness statement.

Synchronized in 0.14

Core checking traverses every installed artifact

The prose now exposes the roots hidden by the compact coreOK equation: top-level code, method and closure bodies, initializer groups, pattern expansions, deferred messages, and recursively derived classes.

What did not change?

Lean did not invent a privileged debugger, collector, parser installer, or exception evaluator. It repeatedly pushed the design back toward the same Newspeak principle: ordinary objects and sends do the work; the VM boundary is limited to representation, allocation, primitive execution, artifact admission, and host services.

02

The whole model

One spine, seven layers

The import graph points downward. Later layers reuse earlier meanings; they do not redefine them. Select a layer to see its job and its main files.

The central state split
PProgramstatic declarations, bodies, mixins, lexical facts
HHeapclasses, objects, activations, closures, mirrors
AActivationsthe stack/control path through live computation

The actor layer gives each actor its own H and active turn; reflection changes P, H, and activation images atomically; collection removes unreachable parts of H without changing strong observations.

03

A five-minute Lean primer

Enough notation to read the model

(p : Program)

“Let p be a Program.” The name is left of the colon; its type is right.

Option ClassId

Either some c or none. It represents genuine absence.

List ClassId

A finite ordered list of class identities.

A → B

A function from A to B. If B is Prop, it is a predicate.

∀ x, P x

For every x, proposition P holds.

∃ x, P x

There exists an x for which P holds.

p.ClassChain h c xs

Dot notation: ClassChain p h c xs, written with the first argument before the dot.

{before after : Config}

Implicit arguments. Lean usually infers them from the explicit evidence.

Example: separate identity typesNewspeak/Id.leanShow Lean

ObjectId and ClassId both contain a natural number, but Lean will not let one be used where the other is expected. That prevents an entire class of semantic bookkeeping errors.

Open the complete file ↗
structure ObjectId where
  index : Nat
deriving Repr, DecidableEq, BEq

structure ClassId where
  index : Nat
deriving Repr, DecidableEq, BEq

inductive ObjRef where
  | ordinaryObject (id : ObjectId)
  | classObject (id : ClassId)
  | mixinObject (id : MixinId)
  | activationObject (id : ActivationId)
  | closureObject (id : ClosureId)
  | mirrorObject (id : MirrorId)
  | actorObject (id : ActorId)
✓
What “machine checked” means: Lean's small trusted kernel has verified that each theorem follows from definitions and earlier theorems. This development contains no sorry, admit, or new axioms.
04

Layer one

The static world and the live world

Program contains declarations and stable code facts. Heap contains live entities. A runtime class record points back to the mixin definition in the Program. This is the hinge on which reflective replacement turns.

P

Program

  • Mixin definitions and method dictionaries
  • Method, closure, and initializer bodies
  • Class/object literal descriptors
  • Lexical parents and scope chains
  • Stable declaration identities
class.mixin→program.mixins
H

Heap

  • Runtime class records
  • Ordinary objects and physical slots
  • Activations and closures
  • Mirrors and actor objects
  • Weak-container payloads
The Program recordNewspeak/Program.leanShow Lean

The fields are the static vocabulary available to all dynamic rules. FiniteStore is a partial map plus an exact, enumerable domain.

Open the complete file ↗
structure Program where
  top : ClassId
  object : ClassId
  mixins : FiniteStore MixinId MixinDef
  methodBodies : FiniteStore MethodId (List Statement)
  closureBodies : FiniteStore ActivationDeclId (List Statement)
  classBodies : FiniteStore ClassDeclId ClassBodyDescriptor
  mixinApplications : FiniteStore ClassDeclId MixinApplicationDescriptor
  objectLiterals : FiniteStore ObjectLiteralDeclId ObjectLiteralDescriptor
  declMixin : FiniteStore ClassBodyDecl MixinId
  lexParent : FiniteStore ClassDeclId ClassDeclId
  scopeChain : SiteId → List ScopeDecl
The Heap recordNewspeak/Heap.leanShow Lean

Each category gets its own store and identity type. Notice that activations and closures are not meta-level machinery; they are runtime records.

Open the complete file ↗
structure Heap where
  classes : FiniteStore ClassId ClassDef
  objects : FiniteStore ObjectId ObjectDef
  mixinObjects : FiniteStore MixinId ClassId
  activations : FiniteStore ActivationId ActivationDef
  closures : FiniteStore ClosureId ClosureDef
  mirrors : FiniteStore MirrorId MirrorDef
  actors : FiniteStore ActorId ActorDef
05

Layer two

Lookup is a walk with three access policies

First establish the unique finite superclass chain. Then scan it according to a mode. Public lookup stops at a protected barrier; protected lookup admits public and protected methods; private methods are skipped except by lexical private selection.

C→B→Object→Top

Accept the first direct definition, regardless of access. This mode is reserved for system lookup such as DNU selection.

The class-chain relationNewspeak/ClassChain.leanShow Lean

An inductive relation can be read as inference rules. A chain is either the singleton [Top], or a class prepended to its parent's valid chain.

Open the complete file ↗
inductive ClassChain (p : Program) (h : Heap) :
    ClassId → List ClassId → Prop where
  | top : ClassChain p h p.top [p.top]
  | step {c parent : ClassId} {tail : List ClassId} :
      c ≠ p.top →
      p.superclass? h c = some parent →
      ClassChain p h parent tail →
      ClassChain p h c (c :: tail)
The executable access policyNewspeak/Lookup.leanShow Lean

The nested Option is intentional. Outer none means “keep searching.” some none means “a protected method blocks public lookup; stop with failure.”

Open the complete file ↗
def lookupAtNonTop (p : Program) (h : Heap)
    (mode : LookupMode) (c : ClassId) (s : Selector) :=
  match p.direct h c s with
  | none => none
  | some method =>
      match mode, method.access with
      | .unrestricted, _ => some (some ⟨method, c⟩)
      | .publicOnly, .publicAccess => some (some ⟨method, c⟩)
      | .publicOnly, .protectedAccess => some none
      | .publicOnly, .privateAccess => none
      | .protectedAccess, .privateAccess => none
      | .protectedAccess, _ => some (some ⟨method, c⟩)

Layer three

The sequential semantics is one relation assembled from disjoint parts

The model does not hide evaluation inside a recursive interpreter. A configuration holds allocation state, the activation stack, and a current control term. Small-step relations describe one observable machine move.

Allocation stateheap + fresh supplies
×
Activation stacklive frames
×
Controlcurrent term
expression orderrequest completionmethod invocationbody machinereturnsclosuresobject slotsclass constructionmessage evaluationfactoryinitializationobject literalsexceptionstuples & patternstop level
The union of core sequential rulesNewspeak/SequentialStep.leanShow Lean

Each constructor embeds one subrelation. Determinism is proved by: same-subrelation cases use that layer's theorem; cross-subrelation cases are impossible because their control shapes differ.

Open the complete file ↗
inductive SequentialStep (p : Program) :
    SequentialConfig → SequentialConfig → Prop where
  | expression : p.ExpressionOrderStep before after →
      p.SequentialStep before after
  | request : p.RequestCompletionStep before after →
      p.SequentialStep before after
  | invocation : p.MethodInvocationStep before after →
      p.SequentialStep before after
  | body : p.BodyMachineStep before after →
      p.SequentialStep before after
  | returns : p.ReturnMachineStep before after →
      p.SequentialStep before after
  | closure : p.ClosureMachineStep before after →
      p.SequentialStep before after
  | objectSlots : p.ObjectSlotStep before after →
      p.SequentialStep before after
  | classes : p.ClassConstructionStep before after →
      p.SequentialStep before after
  | messages : p.MessageEvaluationStep before after →
      p.SequentialStep before after
≠
Why so many disjointness lemmas? A language can have individually deterministic rules yet still be nondeterministic if two different rules both apply to the same state. Lean forced the development to prove that cannot happen.
07

Layer four

Actors lift the whole sequential machine

An actor world contains isolated private heaps, a shared value heap, run states, FIFO mailboxes, network packets, promise/far-reference tables, causal histories, and fresh supplies. Local turns reuse the sequential semantics unchanged.

Actor Aprivate Hₐrunning one turn
eventual send→packet + event→promise
Actor Bprivate HᵦFIFO mailbox
  • Remote representation decides whether an argument crosses as a value, near reference, far reference, or promise.
  • E-order constrains delivery of causally related events without pretending the global scheduler is deterministic.
  • Settlement commits a terminal promise state before emitting wake packets to dependents.
  • Turn determinism is local; actor selection and network interleaving remain genuinely relational choices.
The ActorWorld recordNewspeak/ActorSemantics.leanShow Lean

This is global actor state. More specialized files define routing, turns, transitions, safety, and the determinism of a selected turn.

Open the complete file ↗
structure ActorWorld where
  program : Program
  valueHeap : Heap
  actorAllocations : FiniteStore ActorId AllocationState
  runStates : FiniteStore ActorId ActorRunState
  mailboxes : FiniteStore ActorId (List ActorPacket)
  network : List ActorPacket
  promises : FiniteStore PromiseId PromiseState
  farReferences : FiniteStore FarRefId FarReferenceTarget
  histories : FiniteStore ActorId (List EventId)
  eventLedger : FiniteStore EventId EventRecord
  deliveredEvents : FiniteStore ActorId (List EventId)
  vm : VMId
  programVersion : Nat
  nextActor : Nat
  nextPromise : Nat
  nextFarReference : Nat
  nextEvent : Nat
  nextPauseToken : Nat
08

Layer five

Reflection is an authorized atomic transaction

A transaction can edit source/program structure, class graphs, layouts, individual slots, activation records, continuations, or whole paused stacks. Preparation computes a candidate state; validation checks it; commit changes the world once—or rejection changes nothing.

1Authorizemirror target + right
→
2Preparecandidate world
→
3Validateall invariants
→
4Commitversion +1

Debugger operations are not a separate evaluator. Stack snapshots decode frames into immutable images; replacement materializes fresh/retained activations atomically; resume returns to the ordinary sequential relation. The Simulator must provide a refinement certificate from bytecode frames and PCs to these abstract images.

Validation and the success/failure stepNewspeak/ReflectionTransactions.leanShow Lean

ValidReflection is the conjunction of authorization, preparation, and every semantic validation. ReflectionStep has only commit and reject cases.

Open the complete file ↗
def ValidReflection
    (frontEnd : ReflectionFrontEnd SourceImage)
    (prepareRuntime : ReflectionRuntimePreparation)
    (validate : ReflectionValidator SourceImage)
    (before : ReflectiveVM SourceImage) (requester : ActorId)
    (transaction : List ReflectionCommand)
    (after : ReflectiveVM SourceImage) : Prop :=
  prepareReflection frontEnd prepareRuntime before requester transaction =
      some after ∧
    ReflectionTransactionAuthorized before.world requester transaction ∧
    ReflectionTransactionNonconflicting transaction ∧
    (validate before transaction after).AllHold

inductive ReflectionStep ... where
  | commit : ValidReflection ... before requester transaction after →
      ReflectionStep ... before after
  | reject : rejected state requester transaction failure →
      ReflectionStep ... state state
09

Layer six · optional

Collection is a stuttering refinement

Without the GC layer, heaps grow monotonically. With it, a collection step may remove unreachable records and clear weak observations, but it cannot change any unconditional strong observation of the base semantics.

Rootsprogram · platform · stacks · control · actors · host handles
strong closure ↓
Live₀ordinary slots, classes, frames, messages
ephemeron fixed point ↓
Live*plus WeakMap values whose map and key are live
The atomic collection functionNewspeak/GarbageCollection.leanShow Lean

The function first computes conditional reachability, then restricts every store and clears weak payloads in one transformation. Theorems prove that the resulting live domain is exactly the fixed point.

Open the complete file ↗
def collectHeap (h : Heap) (roots : List ObjRef)
    (nilObject : ObjRef) : Heap :=
  h.collectHeapAtReachability
    (h.conditionallyReachableReferences roots) nilObject

theorem collectHeap_isLiveObject_iff
    (h : Heap) (roots : List ObjRef) (nilObject object : ObjRef) :
    (h.collectHeap roots nilObject).IsLiveObject object ↔
      object ∈ h.conditionallyReachableReferences roots := by
  ...
↺
Why “stuttering”? If you erase GC bookkeeping, a collection step looks like no base-language step at all: the program made no progress, yet its strong observable behavior is unchanged.
10

Layer seven

From characters to annotated core—without a jump

This is the longest bridge in the development because every convenience erased by elaboration must leave behind enough stable identity and annotation for runtime lookup, reflection, debugging, and later recompilation.

  1. 01PEG recognitionsource → concrete tree
  2. 02Semantic projectiontree → surface AST
  3. 03Identificationstable source IDs
  4. 04Surface checksnames, shape, returns
  5. 05Elaborationimplicit syntax → annotated core
  6. 06Program derivationmixins, methods, artifacts
  7. 07Core validationindependent admission check
The composed front-end derivationNewspeak/FrontEnd.leanShow Lean

A successful derivation carries evidence for every stage. The determinism theorem states that the same grammar, input, identity seed, and services cannot produce two different results.

Open the complete file ↗
inductive FrontEndDerivation (grammar : PEGGrammar)
    (decoders : NewspeakLexicalDecoders)
    (derivation : ProgramDerivationServices)
    (retained : IdentityRetentionMap) (supply : IdentificationSupply)
    (source : SourceText) : FrontEndResult → Prop where
  | accepted {surface metadata identification program expression}
      (parsed : PEGParsesNewspeakUnit grammar decoders source
        surface metadata)
      (identified : identifySurfaceCompilationUnit retained supply surface =
        some identification)
      (surfaceValid : derivation.surfaceOK surface identification = true)
      (derived : derivation.deriveProgram surface identification =
        some (program, expression))
      (coreValid : AnnotatedCoreValid program expression
        derivation.coreFuel) :
      FrontEndDerivation grammar decoders derivation retained supply source
        { program := program
          expression := expression
          retention := identification.retention }
The complete static gateNewspeak/CompleteStaticChecking.leanShow Lean

The short LaTeX predicate expands into a recursive executable checker. Its soundness theorem constructs the rich relational evidence used by the rest of the model.

Open the complete file ↗
def completeSurfaceStaticOK
    (config : DirectDerivationConfig)
    (artifactConfig : EmbeddedArtifactConfig) (coreFuel : Nat)
    (unit : SurfaceCompilationUnit)
    (identification : IdentificationOutput) : Bool :=
  surfaceCompilationUnitShapeOK unit &&
    surfaceStaticDeclarationOK config.isUnarySelector unit.declaration &&
    match deriveCompleteClassProgram config artifactConfig
        unit identification with
    | none => false
    | some (program, expression) =>
        annotatedCoreValidCheck program expression coreFuel

theorem completeSurfaceStaticOK_coreValid ... :
    AnnotatedCoreValid program expression coreFuel := by
  unfold completeSurfaceStaticOK at valid
  rw [derived] at valid
  simp only [Bool.and_eq_true] at valid
  exact annotatedCoreValidCheck_sound valid.2
11

The metacircular edge

Ordinary components, extraordinary obligations

A parser or compiler can be changed exactly as other Newspeak code can. What makes its output executable is not its identity or class; it is an admission certificate proving that the produced artifact meets the fixed semantic boundary.

Inside Newspeakparser objectelaborator objectcompiler objectSimulator objectmutable and reflectively replaceable
Admission boundaryparse certificatecore validitycompiled refinementframe/PC correspondencechecked before use
VM parametersdecodingartifact loadingprimitive stepallocation & host I/Ounless separately bootstrapped
Compiled artifact admissionNewspeak/Metacircularity.leanShow Lean

The certificate packages a representation relation and the proof that each concrete instruction step corresponds to zero or more semantic steps. A finite compiled run can therefore be lifted to a finite annotated-core run.

Open the complete file ↗
structure CompiledArtifactAdmission
    (State CodeAddress ProgramCounter : Type)
    (machine : SimulatorMachine State CodeAddress ProgramCounter)
    (decode : SimulatorFrameDecoder CodeAddress ProgramCounter)
    (program : Program) (version : Nat)
    (reifier : ErrorReifier program) where
  certificate : SimulatorRefinementCertificate
    State CodeAddress ProgramCounter machine decode program version reifier

theorem
    CompiledProgramAdmission.execution_refines_annotatedCore ... :
    ∃ semanticAfter,
      program.SequentialExecution reifier admission.semanticInitial
        semanticAfter ∧
      machine.Represents decode program version simulatorAfter
        semanticAfter :=
  admission.artifact.execution_refines
    admission.representsInitial execution

The remaining implementation project: the abstract boundary is proved, but the currently shipped V5 compiler/Simulator pair must still supply the concrete admission certificate. That is implementation verification, not a missing language-semantic rule.

12

A proof, slowly

How to read lookup_deterministic

The theorem says: if two lookup derivations start from the same program, heap, mode, selector, and class, their results are equal. Click through the proof one move at a time.

theorem lookup_deterministic ...
    (h₁ : p.Lookup h mode s start r₁)
    (h₂ : p.Lookup h mode s start r₂) : r₁ = r₂ := by
  rcases h₁ with ⟨chain₁, hc₁, hr₁⟩
  rcases h₂ with ⟨chain₂, hc₂, hr₂⟩
  have hchain : chain₁ = chain₂ := ClassChain.unique hc₁ hc₂
  subst chain₂
  rw [← hr₁, ← hr₂]
1 / 5

State the claim

Two pieces of evidence, h₁ and h₂, say that lookup produced r₁ and r₂ under identical inputs. The goal after the colon is to prove r₁ = r₂.
